title: Parts Promise
user: Solo-to-20-person electricians, HVAC, and repair firms that must promise a job date only when the required part is truly allocated to that job.

evidence.quote_or_summary: A solo carpenter says Jobber cost $150+/month and was bloated for the three needs they actually had: invoicing, scheduling, and client management.

An Ask HN thread specifically asks what has worked when deploying tools in trade or field-service businesses; a responder describes electrical-job workflows across job finding and qualified worker coordination.
The request says aggregate 'on order' quantities do not show whether a specific build/job is covered, forcing manual notes, PO checks, memory, and risking duplicate orders.

recurrence: Tradespeople report price/bloat pressure while a production-inventory user details the same allocation ambiguity that causes repeat purchases and broken customer promises. It arises on every parts-dependent job.
current_workaround: Keep job schedules in field-service software, call suppliers, track parts in spreadsheets or notes, and infer whether generic stock/on-order totals cover the job.
incumbents_and_gap: Jobber, Tradify, ServiceTitan, and ERPs cover broad field service or inventory. The wedge is job-level parts commitment and supplier ETA evidence without buying an enterprise dispatch/ERP stack.
smallest_useful_product: Mobile job card with required-part list, scan/manual allocation from van/warehouse/supplier PO, ETA confidence, customer-date warning, and reorder suggestion. Non-goals: payroll, dispatch optimization, full inventory accounting, or marketplace lead generation.
success_measure: Pilot firms reduce duplicate part orders by 25% and log an attributable parts status for 90% of jobs that require a non-stock item.
monetization: subscription — $39/month base plus $8/technician is tied to daily field use and avoided repeat materials/visits.
constraints: Offline conflict handling, barcode/device permissions, supplier-data licensing, no inaccurate availability guarantees, and regional tax/unit support.
why_distinct: It protects a customer promise through part-to-job attribution rather than cloning a full field-service suite.
